description_ru: Вымышленная новость о женщине, которая поставила личный рекорд и собрала деньги для больницы.
text:
A thirty-four-year-old teacher from the seaside town of Westbay has swum across Silver Bay in just under five hours. Maria Vega, who only learned to swim at the age of twenty-five, raised more than eight thousand pounds for the local children's hospital.

The bay is nearly sixteen kilometres wide, and the water is cold even in summer. Maria began her swim at six o'clock in the morning, accompanied by a small boat with her coach and two volunteers. Thousands of people watched from the beach and along the cliffs, waving flags and cheering.

"The first hour was easy," Maria said afterwards, wrapped in a warm towel. "The second hour was harder. By the third hour, I was thinking about nothing but a hot cup of tea. If my friends had not been shouting my name from the boat, I might have given up."

At one point, a group of dolphins appeared next to her, which the swimmer described as "a very kind surprise". Her coach, Peter Lund, said the animals stayed for about ten minutes.

When she finally reached the other side, the crowd rushed to hug her. Mayor Clara Fisher announced that the town would celebrate with a party on the beach next Saturday.

Asked about her next challenge, Maria laughed. "I have promised my family a long holiday first," she said. "Then I may think about crossing the whole channel. But I need a very large breakfast before I decide."

Doctors at the hospital say the money will buy new equipment for the children's ward.
